claims.statement: Virtual texturing lets a project use large-sized textures with a lower and more consistent runtime memory footprint.

claims.statement: MassEntity is Unreal Engine 5's data-oriented framework for calculations over large numbers of lightweight objects; its primary data structure is the Fragment, an atomic piece of data.

Entities are built by Fragment composition and grouped into Archetypes; entities of an Archetype are stored in memory Chunks so that Fragments can be fetched efficiently, and Processors supply stateless logic queried via EntityQuery.

Because changing an Entity's composition moves it between Archetypes, Processors request composition changes through the MassCommandBuffer, which is batch-processed at the end of the current batch; EntityView provides safe access to other Entities.
MassEntity shipped with Unreal Engine 5.0 (2022).

claims.statement: Occlusion culling prevents Unity from performing rendering calculations for GameObjects that are completely hidden from view by other GameObjects.
Cameras always perform frustum culling, which does not check occlusion; occlusion culling additionally removes Renderers entirely obscured by nearer Renderers.
Unity's built-in occlusion culling performs runtime calculations on the CPU, which can offset the CPU time it saves, so it is most likely to help when the project is GPU-bound due to overdraw.

Occlusion culling data is loaded into memory at runtime, so sufficient memory is required; it works best where small, well-defined areas are separated by solid geometry (e.g. rooms and corridors); dynamic GameObjects can be occluded but cannot occlude others.
